narrations.text: SaaS License Management (SAM Pro). Assigned Seats vs Usage, Reclamation, Connector Health
Classic SaaS waste: 1,000 M365 E5 seats assigned, 260 never signed in 90+ days. That's 26% of spend recoverable — IF your connector data is trustworthy.

On-Premise SAM vs SaaS License Management. Discovery Finds installs on devices Connector pulls subscriptions + assigned seats Metric Per device / core Almost always PER USER / named user Usage Launch metering (SCCM, BigFix) Last activity / sign-in (often stale) Reconciliation Against installs Against ASSIGNED but INACTIVE seats Optimization Uninstall software RECLAIM dormant seats Data Source Agent-based inventory Vendor API (Graph, REST, CSV)

Classic SaaS Waste Pattern. 1,000 assigned M365 E5 seats 260 never signed in for 90+ days 26% of spend recoverable with ZERO user impact IF connector data is trustworthy IF reclaim process has an owner Dead connector = 'no waste' illusion.

Connector Configuration Essentials. API credentials: least-privilege scope Refresh cadence matched to vendor API limits OWNER for each connector (accountability) ALERTING when connector silently stops syncing Dead connector looks exactly like 'no waste'.

Typical SaaS Targets. Microsoft Microsoft 365 (E3/E5/F3) Named user + service plans Salesforce Sales/Service/Platform Cloud Named user + permission sets Adobe Creative Cloud / Document Cloud Named user (VIP/ETLA) Zoom Meetings / Webinars Host licenses Slack Pro / Business+ / Enterprise Grid Active users Workday HCM / Financials Named user ServiceNow ITSM / CSM / HRSD / SAM Pro Fulfilled user / approved requester

SaaS Reconciliation Flow. M365 / Salesforce / Adobe / Zoom ↓ (API: subscriptions + assigned seats) USAGE DATA (last activity, sign-in) ↓ SaaS RECONCILIATION ↓ Under-licensed → TRUE-UP seats Over-licensed → RECLAIM unused seats Compliant → OPTIMIZE allocation Mnemonic: Assigned ≠ Active. Reclaim the gap.
